review_notes: Read the whole file, the definitions of vMinus/vPlus/cycleSlot/transitionSlot/spokeOf/transitionOf in Core.lean and HelperLemma.lean, and the uses of the evaluation lemmas in Gap.lean. I checked the Lean core Fin simprocs (Fin.reduceAdd). I did not run Lean, so I make no claims about simp behaviour that I observed. The proposed bundled simp set and the removal of the redundant simp attributes are untested. I found no rewrite cycle or competing rules in this file.

findings.declaration: Eval section: vMinus_0 … spokeOf_5 (@[simp] evaluation lemmas) and their repeated `simp only` lists in one_le_transitionPathChips, lemma_graad5, five_le_divisorialGonality
findings.problem: The 30 literal-evaluation lemmas are tagged `@[simp]`, but no use in the file or in Gap.lean relies on them being in the default simp set. Every use spells them out again in a long `simp only [...]` list. The same list of about 20 names appears at lines 458-461, 551-556, 561-563 and 597-599, with small differences between copies, and again in Gap.lean (lines 235-237). The list for the `cycleSlot`/`vMinus`/`vPlus`/`fin3_*` names has to be kept in sync by hand each time. The `@[simp]` tags add global rewrites in the generic namespace `Utilities.Tricycle` that nothing exercises, and the interface the proofs actually use is not packaged.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one interface. Either register a dedicated simp set (for example `register_simp_attr tricycle_eval`) and tag these lemmas with it, then write `simp only [tricycle_eval, transitionPathChips, cycleChips, spokePairChips] at ...`. Or keep the default `@[simp]` tags and call plain `simp [transitionPathChips, cycleChips, spokePairChips]`. In either case the repeated 20-name lists disappear. Because the concrete `Fin 15` and `Fin 7` indices form a closed table, a single bundle is enough.
findings.benefit: The normal form for slot and vertex indices (literal `Fin` numerals) is stated once. Later proofs, including those in Gap.lean, stop copying the list and cannot drift apart. The global default simp set no longer carries unused project-specific literal rewrites.

findings.excerpt:
theorem fin3_01 : (0 : Fin 3) + 1 = 1 := by decide
@[simp] theorem fin3_11 : (1 : Fin 3) + 1 = 2 := by decide
findings.problem: The simp attributes are inconsistent and mostly redundant. Four of the six arithmetic facts are `@[simp]` and `fin3_01`, `fin3_02` are not, yet all six are passed to `simp only` and used by `rw` in the same way. The core `Fin.reduceAdd` dsimproc is `[simp]` and already reduces `(1 : Fin 3) + 1` and similar literal sums to numerals, so the `@[simp]` copies duplicate existing coverage. The generic names `fin3_11` etc. are also exported into the default simp set under `Utilities.Tricycle`.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from fin3_11, fin3_21, fin3_12, fin3_22, since the simproc covers them. Where an explicit `simp only` needs them, use `Fin.reduceAdd` in the list (or the bundled set from the previous finding) in place of the six named facts. Keep the named theorems only for the `rw [fin3_02]`-style uses in Gap.lean, and drop the attribute inconsistency.
findings.benefit: This removes the redundant and inconsistent simp coverage and leaves one canonical way to reduce `Fin 3` literal arithmetic. Readers need not wonder why two of the six facts lack `@[simp]`. It also removes a small risk of competing rewrites with the core simproc.
